item.title: Whistleblower claims USPS plan for Trump's mail voting order could 'derail' midterms
item.description: A whistleblower says the U.S. Postal Service is rushing out an online system for President Trump's push to restrict mail voting that could "derail" the midterm election if courts allow it to proceed.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A makeover for college: No gym, no meal plan and two years of work
item.description: A new model in Vermont emphasizes hands-on learning while stripping away frills like gyms and meal plans that increase costs. Other newly created institutions are also reimagining college.

item.title: Judge to decide if Tyler Robinson will go to trial in Charlie Kirk murder case
item.description: Utah District Judge Tony Graf Jr. will hear arguments over evidence introduced in July, to decide if there's enough probable cause for a trial in the shooting of the conservative activist last year.

item.title: Chance for more rain makes rescue operations perilous after Grand Canyon flooding
item.description: Ongoing rain chances are making search and rescue operations at the Grand Canyon more hazardous following Saturday's deadly flooding.

item.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns
item.description: The Army's top civilian leader has resigned. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down after 18 months on the job, the White House says. It's the latest in a series of military leadership shakeups.

item.title: Jury convicts a man of first-degree murder for the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur
item.description: A jury found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, finally bringing a measure of resolution to a case that had gripped hip-hop fans for decades.
